name: italian-pear-nicks

provenance.sourceNotes: Direct family transfer. Continuous selection for 50+ years — selecting for eating quality and sauce performance.

description.preschool: This is the story of a very special tomato seed that has been passed down through a family for over fifty years. The original grower planted these tomatoes in his garden every single year, and every year he picked the very best tomatoes and saved their seeds to plant the next spring. Now those seeds have come to Chico, and we are going to keep the tradition going by saving the best seeds every year too.
description.elementary: Nick's Italian Pear tomato lineage represents over 50 years of careful seed saving in California. Every season, the grower would watch his tomato plants closely and choose the ones that ripened earliest, produced the most fruit, and tasted the best. He saved seeds only from those champion plants, so over the decades his tomatoes got better and better suited to California growing. In 2026, these precious seeds came to Oak Vista in Chico to begin a new chapter — adapting to the hotter, drier Sacramento Valley climate while keeping the excellent flavour selected for over decades.
description.secondary: The Italian Pear (Nick's) seed lineage is a 50+ year continuous phenotypic selection program maintained in coastal California. The selection criteria — earliest ripening, highest production, best flavour — have been applied consistently across an estimated 50 generations, accumulating locally adapted allele frequencies for Mediterranean climate performance. The 2026 season at Oak Vista initiates the Chico climate adaptation phase: selection pressure now includes Sacramento Valley heat tolerance (100–110°F summer peaks) in addition to the established quality criteria. This lineage is irreplaceable — it represents a unique genetic resource that cannot be reconstituted if lost. The seed saving protocol requires fermentation extraction from selected fruit, labelling with date, generation number, and selection criteria, and cool dry storage.
description.university: Italian Pear (Nick's) — a multi-decadal directional selection program on Solanum lycopersicum, paste type, maintained through ~50 generations of continuous seed saving by a single cultivator. The accumulated selection differential across 50+ cycles of phenotypic selection for early maturity, yield, and organoleptic quality represents a significant departure from the founding population's allele frequencies. The genetic architecture is expected to show reduced heterozygosity at loci under selection while maintaining diversity at neutral loci — a signature of sustained directional selection without severe bottlenecking (annual population sizes presumably in the tens of plants). The 2026 Chico adaptation program introduces novel selection pressure: Sacramento Valley thermal regime (Köppen Csa, summer maxima routinely exceeding 38°C) differs substantially from the maritime-moderated coastal California environment (Köppen Csb). Adaptive response to this environmental shift will be monitored through phenological records (days to first ripe fruit, total season yield, fruit quality metrics) across successive Chico generations. Provenance chain integrity is a domain invariant — this lineage must never have a gap in its annual seed saving record.

selectionCriteria: Earliest ripening, highest production, best flavour fruit under Chico Sacramento Valley conditions (100-110°F summer peaks). Select from first flush of ripe fruit for early maturity genes. Label with date, generation number, and selection notes.
notes: HIGHEST PRIORITY seed lineage in the system. Generation 1 of Chico adaptation. 50+ years of continuous selection in coastal California — irreplaceable genetic heritage. Save seeds annually without exception.

name: amish-paste-baker-creek

provenance.sourceNotes: Planned acquisition — source verified open-pollinated seed from Baker Creek (rareseeds.com) if The Plant Barn variety performs well in 2026. Not yet acquired.

description.preschool: If our Amish Paste tomatoes do well this year, we plan to get seeds from a special seed company that makes sure the seeds are the real thing — not a copy. That way we can start saving our own seeds every year and grow these wonderful big sauce tomatoes forever.
description.elementary: The Amish Paste tomatoes we planted in 2026 came from a local nursery, and we are not sure if they are the true open-pollinated variety or a hybrid. If they perform well for sauce making, we plan to order verified open-pollinated Amish Paste seeds from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds — a company that specialises in preserving authentic heirloom vegetable varieties. Once we have confirmed open-pollinated seeds, we can begin saving our own seeds each year.
description.secondary: This planned seed lineage represents the acquisition pathway for verified open-pollinated Amish Paste seed stock from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds (Mansfield, Missouri). The 2026 Oak Vista planting uses nursery starts from The Plant Barn (Chico CA) with unconfirmed breeding status — potentially hybrid. If the 2026 crop demonstrates satisfactory sauce quality and heat tolerance, Baker Creek OP seed will be sourced for the 2027 season to establish a genuine seed saving program. Baker Creek maintains isolation protocols for their open-pollinated varieties, providing reasonable assurance of genetic integrity.
description.university: Planned acquisition of verified Solanum lycopersicum 'Amish Paste' open-pollinated seed stock from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds. Baker Creek maintains variety isolation distances (minimum 10 m for self-pollinating Solanaceae, though tomato outcrossing rates of 2–5% in field conditions suggest longer distances are prudent) and conducts grow-out trials for trueness-to-type verification. The 2026 evaluation season at Oak Vista will establish baseline performance data (yield per plant, Brix, sauce conversion ratio, days to maturity) against which the Baker Creek stock can be compared in 2027. If both sources prove true-to-type, the higher-performing stock under Chico conditions becomes the founding population for local adaptation. Estimated generations set to 0 — lineage not yet initiated.

notes: Planned lineage — not yet active. Contingent on 2026 Amish Paste performance evaluation and Baker Creek seed acquisition. Will activate if variety proves suitable for 90-quart sauce production target.

name: genovese-basil-oak-vista

provenance.sourceNotes: Seed saved from 2025 Oak Vista planting. Original stock from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds verified open-pollinated Genovese. First generation of local selection under Sacramento Valley conditions.

description.preschool: We saved seeds from our very best basil plants — the ones that grew the biggest, tastiest leaves and did not flower too quickly in the hot Chico summer. Next year we will plant those seeds and do it again!
description.elementary: Genovese basil is the classic Italian cooking basil with large, fragrant leaves perfect for pesto and caprese. In 2025 we started saving seeds from the plants that held off flowering the longest in Chico's extreme summer heat. Basil wants to bolt — rush to make flowers and seeds — when it gets very hot, so we are selecting for plants that keep making delicious leaves even when temperatures hit 105°F.
description.secondary: This seed lineage tracks the local adaptation of Ocimum basilicum 'Genovese' to Sacramento Valley growing conditions at Oak Vista (Chico, CA). The primary selection pressure is bolt resistance under sustained high temperatures (38–43°C daily maxima, June through September). Genovese basil is a short-day-neutral annual that initiates flowering in response to heat stress and photoperiod signals. Selection for delayed bolting effectively selects for elevated heat shock protein expression thresholds and modified photoperiod sensitivity. Secondary criteria include leaf size, essential oil concentration (assessed organoleptically), and Fusarium wilt tolerance.
description.university: Ocimum basilicum 'Genovese' local adaptation program, Generation 1. Founding population sourced from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds verified open-pollinated stock. Basil is predominantly self-pollinating (cleistogamous flower structure) with outcrossing rates of 5–15% mediated by hymenopteran visitors, making it amenable to mass selection without strict isolation. Selection differential applied against premature reproductive transition (bolting) under Sacramento Valley thermal regime — sustained maxima exceeding 38°C trigger ethylene-mediated floral induction in basil, and the selection target is elevated thermal thresholds for this transition. The quantitative genetics of bolt resistance in basil suggest moderate heritability (h² ≈ 0.3–0.5 based on analogous Lamiaceae studies), so meaningful response to selection is expected within 3–5 generations. Essential oil profile (linalool:eugenol ratio characteristic of Genovese type) will be monitored to prevent drift from the culinary chemotype under heat-stress selection.

selectionCriteria: Latest bolting under Sacramento Valley heat (100-110°F). Select plants that maintain vegetative growth longest. Secondary: leaf size, aroma intensity, Fusarium tolerance.
notes: Generation 1 of Chico adaptation. Basil is predominantly self-pollinating — isolation distances less critical than for cross-pollinating crops. Save seed from 5+ plants minimum to maintain genetic diversity.

name: thai-basil-oak-vista

provenance.sourceNotes: Seed saved from 2025 Oak Vista planting. Original stock from local nursery start — variety confirmed as Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora by floral morphology (purple inflorescence, anise-clove aroma profile).

description.preschool: Thai basil smells like liquorice and has pretty purple flowers. We saved seeds from the toughest plants that kept growing even in the hottest part of summer. Thai basil handles heat better than Italian basil, so it is a great one for Chico gardens.
description.elementary: Thai basil is a different kind of basil with a spicy anise-liquorice flavour used in Southeast Asian cooking — stir fries, curries, and pho. It naturally handles heat better than Genovese basil because it evolved in tropical climates. We are still selecting the very best plants each year: the ones with the most aromatic leaves, the strongest stems, and the best flavour for cooking.
description.secondary: Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora local adaptation at Oak Vista. Thai basil carries inherently higher heat tolerance than sweet basil cultivars, reflecting its tropical Southeast Asian origin and adaptation to equatorial photoperiods and sustained high temperatures. Selection criteria at Chico focus on aromatic compound concentration (the characteristic estragole-dominated essential oil profile that distinguishes Thai basil from sweet basil chemotypes), stem rigidity for upright growth habit, and sustained vegetative production through the full Sacramento Valley growing season (April–October). The purple inflorescence is both a cultivar marker and a pollinator attractant — Thai basil flowers are heavily visited by carpenter bees (Xylocopa) and honeybees.
description.university: Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora, Generation 1 local adaptation. Thai basil's essential oil profile is dominated by estragole (methyl chavicol, 60–80% of volatile fraction) versus the linalool-dominant profile of Genovese types — this chemotypic difference is under simple genetic control (the eugenol O-methyltransferase pathway) and must be maintained under selection to preserve culinary identity. The variety's tropical origin (likely Indochinese center of diversity) confers pre-adaptation to high temperature regimes, but the Sacramento Valley's Mediterranean seasonality (cool wet winters, hot dry summers) differs from the equatorial wet-dry pattern. Selection will monitor phenological response to this novel photoperiod-temperature combination. Outcrossing between Thai basil and Genovese basil planted in proximity is a concern — while basil is predominantly autogamous, the 5–15% outcrossing rate could introgress linalool-pathway alleles into the estragole chemotype. Minimum 30m isolation or temporal isolation (staggered flowering) is recommended.

selectionCriteria: Aroma intensity (estragole-dominant profile), stem rigidity, sustained production through full Sacramento Valley season. Maintain chemotype distinction from sweet basil — monitor for linalool introgression if planted near Genovese.
notes: Generation 1 of Chico adaptation. Higher inherent heat tolerance than sweet basil. Isolation from Genovese basil planting recommended to maintain chemotype purity — minimum 30m or stagger flowering periods.

name: italian-flat-leaf-parsley-oak-vista

provenance.sourceNotes: Seed saved from 2025 Oak Vista planting. Original stock from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds verified open-pollinated Italian Giant variety. Biennial — seed harvested in second year from overwintered plants.

description.preschool: Parsley is a plant that takes two whole years to make seeds. The first year it grows lots of flat, tasty leaves we use in cooking. The second year it sends up a tall flower stalk covered in tiny white flowers that bees love. We save seeds from the plants with the most flavour and the biggest, darkest green leaves.
description.elementary: Italian flat-leaf parsley is a biennial herb — it lives for two years. The first year it makes a rosette of flat, deeply flavoured leaves used in everything from chimichurri to tabbouleh. The second year, the plant bolts — sending up tall umbel flower stalks that attract beneficial insects like parasitic wasps and hoverflies. We let these flower stalks produce seeds, then harvest and dry them for next year's planting. Because parsley is biennial, seed saving requires overwintering the plants — Chico's mild winters make this straightforward.
description.secondary: Petroselinum crispum var. neapolitanum local adaptation, Generation 1. Italian flat-leaf parsley is biennial — vernalisation (exposure to temperatures below 10°C for 6–8 weeks) triggers the transition from vegetative rosette to reproductive bolt in the second year. Chico's winter temperatures (average January minimum ~3°C) provide adequate vernalisation without killing the plant. Selection criteria focus on leaf size, essential oil concentration (the characteristic petroselinic acid and myristicin profile that gives flat-leaf parsley its superior flavour over curled varieties), and bolt resistance in the first year — premature bolting before the second spring wastes the vegetative harvest. As an Apiaceae, parsley is insect-pollinated and obligately outcrossing (protandrous flowers prevent selfing), requiring isolation from curled parsley varieties to maintain the flat-leaf chemotype.
description.university: Petroselinum crispum var. neapolitanum, Generation 1 biennial seed saving program. Parsley is an obligate outcrosser (protandrous dichogamy in Apiaceae) with pollination mediated by small hymenopterans and Diptera attracted to the compound umbel inflorescence. The outcrossing requirement means minimum effective population size for seed saving is higher than for autogamous crops — recommend 10+ plants for adequate genetic diversity and avoidance of inbreeding depression. Isolation distance from P. crispum var. crispum (curled parsley) should be minimum 400m to prevent gene flow that would compromise the flat-leaf morphology and neapolitanum essential oil profile. The biennial life cycle introduces a generation time constraint — response to selection operates on a 2-year cycle, so adaptation will proceed at half the rate of annual crops. Vernalisation requirement (6–8 weeks below 10°C, quantitative response) is reliably met in Chico (USDA Zone 9b, ~800 chill hours). Seed viability in Apiaceae declines rapidly — use seed within 1–2 years of harvest.

selectionCriteria: Leaf size, dark green colour, flavour intensity (petroselinic acid profile), bolt resistance in first year. Mark best vegetative plants in year one for overwintering and seed harvest in year two.
notes: Biennial crop — 2-year generation cycle. Obligate outcrosser requiring 10+ plants for genetic diversity. Isolate from curled parsley varieties (400m minimum). Chico winters adequate for vernalisation.

name: black-beauty-eggplant-oak-vista

provenance.sourceNotes: Seed saved from 2025 Oak Vista planting. Original stock from certified organic nursery starts. Black Beauty is an heirloom open-pollinated variety dating to 1902 — one of the oldest commercially available eggplant cultivars.

description.preschool: Eggplants love hot weather, and Chico summers are exactly what they want! Black Beauty eggplants are big, shiny, and dark purple. We save seeds from the biggest, shiniest fruits that grew on the healthiest plants. The seeds are tiny and flat — we scoop them out and dry them for next year.
description.elementary: Black Beauty is one of the oldest eggplant varieties — it has been grown since 1902. It produces large, glossy, dark purple fruits that are perfect for grilling, baking, and making eggplant parmesan. Eggplants are tropical plants that thrive in Chico's hot summers, but they can struggle with flea beetles and verticillium wilt. We select seeds from the plants that produce the most fruit while staying healthy through the whole season, especially looking for any natural resistance to pest damage.
description.secondary: Solanum melongena 'Black Beauty' local adaptation at Oak Vista. Black Beauty is an heirloom open-pollinated cultivar introduced in 1902, predating modern hybrid breeding programs. As a Solanaceae member, eggplant is predominantly self-pollinating (cleistogamous to partially chasmogamous flowers) with outcrossing rates of 5–20% depending on pollinator activity — higher than tomato due to the larger, more accessible floral structure. Selection criteria at Chico target fruit yield, glossy skin quality (anthocyanin concentration in the exocarp), and tolerance to the two primary Sacramento Valley production challenges: Epitrix hirtipennis (eggplant flea beetle) feeding damage and Verticillium dahliae soilborne infection. The 100–110°F summer temperatures are ideal for eggplant — fruit set improves with heat, unlike tomato which drops pollen above 95°F.
description.university: Solanum melongena 'Black Beauty', Generation 1 local adaptation. This 1902 heirloom cultivar represents a pre-Green Revolution gene pool maintained through over a century of open-pollinated propagation. The anthocyanin profile (primarily nasunin, a delphinidin-based compound) responsible for the characteristic dark purple exocarp is under relatively simple genetic control and should remain stable under selection for agronomic traits. Eggplant's outcrossing rate of 5–20% (mediated primarily by Bombus spp. and Xylocopa spp.) is sufficient to maintain heterozygosity but low enough to permit mass selection without strict isolation — though 50m separation from other S. melongena cultivars is recommended to preserve Black Beauty's phenotype. Key selection targets: quantitative resistance to Verticillium dahliae race 1 (the predominant Sacramento Valley pathotype), reduced Epitrix feeding preference (trichome density and glycoalkaloid concentration in foliage are candidate resistance mechanisms), and sustained fruit production under high temperature and low humidity conditions characteristic of Chico's Mediterranean climate.

selectionCriteria: Fruit yield, glossy dark purple skin, Verticillium wilt tolerance, flea beetle resistance. Eggplant thrives in Chico heat — select for sustained production through full summer. Save seed from overripe fruit left on the plant until skin turns dull brown-yellow.
notes: Generation 1 of Chico adaptation. Eggplant excels in Sacramento Valley heat — one of the few Solanaceae that improves with extreme temperatures. Flea beetle management is the primary production challenge. Save seed from 3+ plants minimum.
